title: The file enum on `edit` and `st edit` is declared and nothing enforces it
body:
**RESTORED ARCHAEOLOGY, TRANSCRIBED VERBATIM ON 2026-08-31.** This issue was filed with an empty body because no verb could write one -- the defect `0090` names -- so its finding survived only in the commit that filed it. The prose below is its author's, carried whole from `a6e336a7` (*feat(0057/05): the lifecycle verbs edit the list, and `intent edit` is one home*). **Nothing in it is written by the restorer**; the header you are reading is the only addition, and the commit's hard line wraps are joined without a word changed.

hv's rulings 2 and 3. AC-05.2 and AC-05.1/05.3.

RULING 2 -- the list edit, keyed on the OP and never on the status. `st new` adds the entry and `--dehydrate` does not; `st done` and `st cancel` remove it and `--keep` does not; `st reopen` and `st reinstate` add it back. Keying on the op is arithmetic rather than principle: `st.triage` and `st.reinstate` both land on NotStarted, and `st.start`, `st.resume` and `st.reopen` all land on Wip, so a match on the destination makes `st triage` start listing threads and `st start` re-add one a human removed. Two collisions in a vocabulary of eight.

The edit runs AFTER `apply`, chosen for its failure mode. Both orders can be interrupted between the two writes; manifest-first leaves a live thread marked not-realised and the next `organize` removes its files, while store-first leaves a closed thread listed -- which is exactly what `--keep` asks for on purpose. One order degrades into a supported outcome and the other into a deletion nobody asked for.

ABSENT IS NOT EMPTY, so no verb creates the manifest: a missing file means everything is realised, and creating one to hold a single entry would declare that entry the whole of what is realised. Any io error other than NotFound is raised -- an unreadable file answering as "nobody has said" is the No Silent Errors case exactly.

hv ruled the `st cancel --keep` asymmetry OUT. AC-05.2 named only `st done --keep` and the guess that the silence was deliberate was wrong: `--keep` is not about how sure you are the work is over, it is about whether you still need to READ the files, and a cancelled thread is at least as likely to be one you are still mining. Both verbs now take it, and a test asserts they AGREE rather than that each is right alone.

The closing note comes from `sync_uncommitted`, read before the write, and is tied to the REMOVAL rather than the verb -- `--keep` cancels the dehydration, so there is nothing to warn about. `Outcome::MovedWith` carries it and `reported()` prints it: a new variant would NOT force the nineteen renderer arms, which all ask `already()`, a method that absorbs a variant in silence. What makes a note undroppable is the single reporter, not the enum.

RULING 3 -- `intent edit <address>` promotes a bare id, hydrates, and prints a path that EXISTS. v2 printed one whether or not anything was there. A generated view is REFUSED and the refusal names where to author (hv, 2026-08-19) -- detection is not prevention, and the skew check catches a hand-edited view after the work is gone. `st edit` delegates, and a source-level check counts the call sites, because Highlander is a claim about how many implementations exist and only a count can go red when a second one appears.

The `file` vocabulary is now ENFORCED, read from the table via `dispatch::arg_values` rather than restated. Not a clap `value_parser`: clap rejects at exit 2, which is INV-04's usage code and the one the pre-commit gate fails open on. Issue 0062 recorded the gap and is closed by this rather than carried.

`intent/.intentfiles` stops documenting the ISSUE sigil that ruling 1 deleted -- the file's own example instructed a reader to write a line that now aborts the run.

Four mutants, each reddening exactly one test and only that one: triage/ start keyed Add, hold/resume keyed Remove, NotFound creating the file, and the list edit hoisted ahead of the self-loop return. Driven in a detached worktree rather than by copying a shared source aside.

Workspace 964 pass / 0 fail over 137 targets with --no-fail-fast.
